item.title: A farming ‘fairy tale’ for modern times | Sustainable Food Trust
item.description: With Christmas approaching – a time for stories and renewed hope – Robert Barbour, Senior Research Manager at the Sustainable Food Trust, reflects on the six months since the launch of Grazing Livestock: It’s not the cow but the how.

item.title: Food on trial: Are ultra-processed foods facing their ‘Big Tobacco’ moment? | Sustainable Food Trust
item.description: We take a look at the evidence behind the health risks, cultural impacts and rising scrutiny of ultra-processed foods.

item.title: Chemicals on the plate: A conversation about food and health | Sustainable Food Trust
item.description: What’s really in our food these days and how might it be affecting our health? We discuss what chemical residues and ultra-processed foods might mean for our health, and consider possible solutions.

item.title: Reflections from ORFC | Sustainable Food Trust
item.description: The SFT team reflects on the 2026 Oxford Real Farming Conference, highlighting notable sessions, workshops and conversations that took place.

item.title: Is prison food finally getting an upgrade? | Sustainable Food Trust
item.description: In February 2026, a new Prison Food Policy framework comes into force for all prisons across England and Wales. SFT's Senior Research Officer, Imogen Crossland, takes a closer look at the framework and explores what it could mean for the quality and procurement of the food served in prisons.

item.title: Can the UK feed itself in the face of ecosystem collapse? New security report gives stark warnings | Sustainable Food Trust
item.description: Our Head of Policy & Campaigns, Megan Perry, explores the UK Government's recently published security report, highlighting how the government's ‘just in time’ approach to food supply jeopardises the UK's food security.

item.title: The weakening link between our local abattoirs, organic meat and high animal welfare | Sustainable Food Trust
item.description: In the 1970s there were 2,500 abattoirs in the UK – today there are only 203. Wicked Leeks’s Anna Zuurmond takes a closer look at the ways in which farmers have been affected by the loss of their local abattoir, as well as what this means for consumers and access to higher-welfare, organic meat.

item.title: The Harmony Debates: Foreword by King Charles III | Sustainable Food Trust
item.description: To mark this Harmony edition of the SFT Newsletter, we're sharing our Patron, King Charles III's foreword from 'The Harmony Debates: Exploring a Practical Philosophy for a Sustainable Future', which was also delivered by HRH as a speech at the Sustainable Food Trust's Harmony in Food and Farming Conference in July 2017.

item.title: Lebanon’s food crisis shows why resilient local food systems matter | Sustainable Food Trust
item.description: As conflict and climate change cause increasing turmoil and food security rises up the global agenda, Zeead Yaghi – scholar, writer and editor – explores why Lebanon is at such severe risk of food shortages and the lessons that can be learned.

item.title: Built on inputs not resilience: The UK’s food security problem | Sustainable Food Trust
item.description: Reflecting on current situation in the Middle East and the subsequent impact on food security around the world, the SFT's research team imagine what a future food system that's more resilient to global shocks and price volatility might look like.

item.title: Beacon Farms: Reflections on our first year of school visits | Sustainable Food Trust
item.description: We reflect on the success of our school visits delivered as part of our Beacon Farms project – 10 Beacon Farms have delivered 75 school visits for more than 1,800 primary aged children, many of whom had never visited a farm before.

item.title: Making more of your meal: Christmas pudding | Sustainable Food Trust
item.description: We look at some staple meals, considering how you can put a healthy, sustainable and more local spin on them – this time: Christmas pudding!
